brief.reader: A strong eight-year-old learning the source lesson in Chinese or English.
brief.jobStory: When I see several colored bands made by a grating, I want to follow how the slit spacing and wave travel determine their directions, so I can explain the central band and the separated spectra.
brief.question: Why does a diffraction grating send reinforcing light into particular directions?
brief.basis: Direct human audience instruction and the closed d915 source requirements.
brief.structure: Retain every assembled prose object in source order. Explain the apparatus, spacing, path difference, principal orders, corresponding slit points, focal-plane observation, white light, wavelength measurement, and the original everyday observations.

en: **Grating spacing and wavelength.**
**Path difference.**
**Principal maxima and orders.**
**Bright bands on the screen.**
**White light and spectra.**
**Measuring wavelength.**
**Grating effects in everyday objects.**

zh: **衍射光栅**利用许多靠得很近的狭缝，让光波展开并相互叠加。
衍射是波通过狭缝或经过边缘后，向直线光路以外展开的现象。
透射光栅由大量很窄的平行狭缝组成，相邻狭缝之间是不透明的条纹（图 206）。
狭缝让光通过，不透明条纹挡住光，许多狭缝一起决定最后的明暗图样。
图中的放大镜帮助我们看清密集的平行条纹，不是增加了一组狭缝。
原书介绍，专门的刻划机可以在玻璃平板上刻出平行细线，每 1 毫米可达几千条。
细线总数可以超过 100000 条，所以光栅有许多重复排列的部分。
原书还介绍了夹在两块玻璃平板之间的白明胶光栅印痕。
光栅也可以利用反射光，而不让光穿过玻璃。
原书称**反射光栅**具有最好的质量，并描述了交替反射光和散射光的条纹。
其中散射光的条纹用雕刻刀在磨光的金属平板上刻出。
透射与反射是两种结构，重复的条纹使来自不同位置的波能够相互配合。
en: A **diffraction grating** uses many closely spaced slits to spread light waves and let them combine.
Diffraction is the spreading of a wave beyond its straight-ahead path after an opening or an edge.
A transmission grating has many narrow, parallel slits separated by opaque strips, as in Figure 206.
The slits transmit light, while the opaque strips block it.
Light from all the slits combines to determine the pattern of brightness.
The magnifying glass makes the closely spaced parallel strips easier to see; it does not add another set of slits.
The source describes a special ruling machine making parallel lines on a glass plate, with several thousand lines in every 1 millimeter.
The total can exceed 100000 lines, giving the grating many repeating parts.
The source also describes a white-gelatin grating impression held between two glass plates.
A grating can use reflected light instead of transmitting light through glass.
The source calls **reflection gratings** the highest-quality type and describes alternating reflecting and scattering strips.
The scattering strips are cut into a polished metal plate with a cutting tool.
Transmission and reflection are different arrangements, but repeated strips allow waves from different positions to combine.
p0236#8.basis: p0236#8 continues transparently through the two figures and captions into p0237#5. Retain the construction, all original numbers, white-gelatin wording, and reflecting/scattering distinction. Attribute the source's highest-quality judgment rather than presenting it as a newly verified universal ranking. Magnifier semantics come from the inspected fig-206 PNG.

zh: **光栅间距和波长**：透明狭缝的宽度记作 $a$，不透明间隔的宽度记作 $b$。
在反射光栅中，它们分别对应反射光条纹和散射光条纹的宽度。
这两段宽度加起来就是 $d=a+b$，称为**光栅常数**，也就是光栅重复一次的间距。
它是从一条狭缝的某个位置到下一条狭缝相应位置的距离，不是狭缝之间空隙单独的宽度。
现在让波长为 $\lambda$ 的平行单色光射到光栅上（图 207）。
波长是波沿传播方向重复一次的距离，可以把它理解为相邻两个同样波动状态之间的距离。
单色在这个模型中表示只有一种波长，平行表示入射光的传播方向相同。
图中入射光垂直照到光栅，下面的推导采用这种正入射和均匀间距。
光栅间距属于光栅本身，波长属于入射光，屏幕到光栅的距离则是另一种距离。
en: **Grating spacing and wavelength.** Let $a$ be the width of a transparent slit and $b$ the width of the opaque interval beside it.
For a reflection grating, these are the widths of the reflecting and scattering strips.
Their sum, $d=a+b$, is the **grating spacing**, also called the grating constant.
It is the distance from a position in one slit to the corresponding position in the next slit.
It is not just the width of the opaque interval.
Now let parallel, monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ fall on the grating in Figure 207.
Wavelength is the distance over which the wave repeats along its direction of travel.
Think of the distance between neighboring positions at the same stage of the wave.
Monochromatic means a single wavelength in this model, and parallel means the incoming directions are the same.
The diagram shows light arriving perpendicular to the grating.
The following derivation uses this normal incidence and uniformly spaced slits.
Grating spacing belongs to the apparatus, wavelength belongs to the light, and the distance to the screen is a different distance.
p0237#6.basis: Retain ordered literal tokens a, b, d=a+b, lambda and Figure 207. Define repeat distance, wavelength, monochromatic and parallel. Normal incidence is a diagram-supported assumption, not an added oblique-incidence formula.

zh: **光程差**：把狭缝上的各处看作发出次波的位置，这些光波向不同方向展开。
次波是描述原来的光怎样传播的波动模型，不是狭缝自己产生了新的灯光。
我们考察与正前方夹角为 $\varphi$ 的一个传播方向，正前方就是垂直于光栅的方向。
图里从相邻狭缝对应边缘发出的两条光线彼此平行，它们到达同一个比较波面时，走过的路程不同。
这段路程之差等于线段 $AC$ 的长度，称为光程差。
如果 $AC$ 的长度是波长的整数倍，一列波比另一列多走的正好是完整的波动周期。
两列波到达时仍处在相同的振动阶段，也就是相位相同，因此彼此加强。
这里依靠的是同一束入射光和规则间距，不是任意互不相关的光源都会这样配合。
图中的 A 和 B 是相邻狭缝的对应边缘，B 到 C 的辅助线垂直于出射光线，C 在从 A 出发的光线上。
这样得到直角三角形 $ABC$，可以求出表示程差的直角边。
en: **Path difference.** Treat positions across the slits as sources of secondary waves spreading in different directions.
These secondary waves describe how the incoming light propagates; the slits are not new lamps.
Consider a direction at angle $\varphi$ to straight ahead, the direction perpendicular to the grating.
The diagram shows parallel rays from corresponding edges of neighboring slits.
They travel different distances before reaching the same comparison wavefront.
The extra distance is the length of segment $AC$, called the path difference.
If $AC$ is an integer number of wavelengths long, one wave travels an extra whole number of cycles.
The waves still arrive at the same stage of oscillation, or the same phase, so they reinforce one another.
This uses the common incoming beam and regular spacing, not unrelated light sources.
A and B mark corresponding edges of adjacent slits.
The helper line from B to C is perpendicular to the outgoing rays, and C lies on the ray from A.
This makes the right triangle $ABC$, from which we can find the leg representing the path difference.
p0237#7.basis: Retain ordered phi, AC, AC, ABC tokens. Inspect fig-207 to identify corresponding lower edges, parallel outgoing rays, perpendicular BC and right-angle geometry. Explain phase and common illumination without inventing a numerical example.

zh: 程差是相邻狭缝间距在出射方向上的投影。
三角形中的正弦表示对边长度与斜边长度的比，因此有：
$|AC|=|AB|\sin\varphi=d\sin\varphi$。
式中的光栅间距是斜边长度，程差是对着观察角的直角边长度。
沿正前方观察时，两条光线没有这段额外路程，向侧方观察才出现程差。
角度与距离是不同的量，正弦帮助我们从角度求出相应的长度比例。
en: The path difference is the projection of the spacing between adjacent slits onto the outgoing direction.
In a right triangle, sine is the ratio of the opposite leg to the hypotenuse, so:
$|AC|=|AB|\sin\varphi=d\sin\varphi$.
Here the grating spacing is the hypotenuse length, and the path difference is the leg opposite the viewing angle.
Looking straight ahead gives no extra path length between the two rays.
Looking to the side produces a path difference.
An angle is not a distance; sine lets us use the angle to find a length ratio.
p0237#8.basis: Preserve the complete original formula exactly. Explain sine as a right-triangle ratio and the distinction between a physical distance and an angle. No extra equation or approximate small-angle replacement.

zh: **主最大值和级次**：有些方向的波彼此加强，形成明显的亮纹，也就是强度的最大值。
这些方向的角度记作 $\varphi$。
把程差等于整倍波长的条件写出来，就能确定角 $\varphi$：
$d\sin\varphi=k\lambda$（7.9）。
其中 $k=0,1,2\cdots\cdots$，这些最大值叫做**主最大值**。
级次表示程差包含多少个完整波长，它是整数，不是任意连续变化的数。
零级沿正前方，程差为零；一级的程差是一个波长，二级是两个波长。
本书用非负级次列出中心和一侧的顺序，相同入射条件下，另一侧也有对应方向。
只有这个关系能给出真实传播方向时，该级次才在几何上允许；正弦的大小不能超过一。
所以级次不能无限增大，允许多少级要同时看光栅间距和波长。
en: **Principal maxima and orders.** In certain directions the waves reinforce one another, making prominent bright bands, or intensity maxima.
Write the angle of such a direction as $\varphi$.
Requiring the path difference to be a whole number of wavelengths determines angle $\varphi$:
$d\sin\varphi=k\lambda$ (7.9).
Here $k=0,1,2\cdots\cdots$, and these maxima are called **principal maxima**.
The order counts the whole wavelengths in the path difference, so it is an integer rather than any continuously variable number.
The zero order points straight ahead and has no path difference.
The first order has an extra wavelength, and the second order has two.
The source lists nonnegative orders for the center and one side.
Under the same incidence, matching directions occur on the other side.
An order is geometrically allowed only when the relation gives a real propagation direction, since the magnitude of sine cannot exceed one.
Orders therefore cannot increase without limit; the available orders depend on both grating spacing and wavelength.
p0237#9.basis: p0237#9 continues into p0238#1. Preserve phi, phi, the exact grating equation, its label (7.9), and the exact nonnegative k list. Explain order, bilateral normal-incidence symmetry and the sine bound in words, with no signed-order rewrite or extra numerical task.

zh: 式（7.9）的条件不只适用于图中狭缝的下边缘。
在相邻狭缝内选取同样相对位置的点，它们的间距都是 $d$。
这些对应点的次波也有 $k\lambda$ 的程差，因此相互加强。
可以把一条狭缝的各个位置与下一条狭缝的相应位置配对，整条狭缝的光都参与叠加。
这说明为什么边缘三角形能够代表不同狭缝之间的加强条件。
不过，同一条狭缝内部不同位置发出的波也要叠加，这会影响各级亮纹的强弱。
某些几何上允许的级次可以很弱，甚至受到单缝衍射的抵消，所以主最大值条件不保证每级都同样亮。
en: Condition (7.9) applies beyond the lower slit edges drawn in the diagram.
Points at matching positions within neighboring slits are separated by $d$.
Their secondary waves also have path difference $k\lambda$, so they reinforce one another.
Each position across one slit has a corresponding position across the next slit, and light from the whole slit contributes.
This is why the edge triangle represents the reinforcement condition between different slits.
Waves from different positions within a single slit must also combine, however, and this affects the strength of each order.
Some geometrically allowed orders may be weak or even canceled by single-slit diffraction.
The principal-maximum condition does not guarantee equally bright orders.
p0238#2.basis: Retain (7.9), d, k lambda and the source's corresponding-point argument. Distinguish reinforcement between slits from the single-slit contribution to total intensity; this authored model qualification is not a silent correction to the source equation.

zh: **屏幕上的亮纹**：把会聚透镜放在光栅后面，再把屏幕放在透镜的焦平面上。
焦平面是透镜把来自同一方向的平行光会聚到点的位置所组成的平面，不是任意放置屏幕的地方。
透镜把图中同一出射方向的光线会聚到屏幕上的同一点，让它们在那里叠加。
满足式（7.9）条件的各个角 $\varphi$，决定相应亮纹在屏幕上的位置。
透镜改变光线的后续路径，却没有把光栅上的狭缝间距变成屏幕上的亮纹间距。
离正前方更远的方向，在焦平面上对应离中心更远的位置。
从角度换成屏幕上的具体长度还需要透镜的焦距，不能只用光栅间距代替。
en: **Bright bands on the screen.** Place a converging lens behind the grating and put the screen in its focal plane.
The focal plane contains the points where the lens brings parallel rays from each direction together.
It is a specific plane, not an arbitrary screen position.
The lens brings rays traveling in the same outgoing direction to the same point on the screen, where their waves combine.
The angles $\varphi$ satisfying condition (7.9) determine the positions of the corresponding bright bands.
The lens changes the later paths of the rays; it does not turn slit spacing into the spacing between bands on the screen.
A direction farther from straight ahead reaches a position farther from the center in the focal plane.
Finding an actual distance on that screen also requires the lens focal length, not just the grating spacing.
p0238#3.basis: Retain source lens-after-grating, screen-in-focal-plane, (7.9) and phi. Explain the directional focusing shown by inspected fig-207 and distinguish apparatus spacing, screen position and focal length. No invented distance or focal-length formula.

zh: **白光和光谱**：白光包含不同波长的光。
除了对应 $k=0$ 的中心最大值，亮纹位置会随波长改变，所以光栅能把白光分成光谱（彩图 IV,1）。
中心方向的程差为零，不同波长都能在这个方向加强，因此零级不会像侧面的级次那样把颜色分开。
在同一级次、同一光栅的条件下，$\lambda$ 越大，最大值就离中心最大值越远（彩图 IV2,3）。
比较波长时必须固定级次，不能把不同级次的亮纹当成同一次比较。
对于 $k$ 的每个非零允许值，都有相应的光谱；中心零级则是不同波长重合的亮纹。
实际观察中不同级次的光谱也可能重叠，这不表示光栅把一种波长变成了另一种。
这里的彩图编号仍指原书彩图，不代表另有一张已经提供的现代彩图。
en: **White light and spectra.** White light contains light of different wavelengths.
Except for the central maximum corresponding to $k=0$, maximum positions depend on wavelength, so a grating separates white light into a spectrum (color plate IV,1).
The path difference is zero straight ahead, allowing different wavelengths to reinforce in the central direction.
The zero order therefore does not separate colors as the side orders do.
For the same grating and the same order, a larger $\lambda$ puts the maximum farther from the central maximum (color plate IV2,3).
Keep the order fixed when comparing wavelengths; bands of different orders are not the same comparison.
Each allowed nonzero value of $k$ has its corresponding spectrum, while the central zero order combines wavelengths in one bright band.
Spectra of different orders can overlap in an observation.
That does not mean the grating changes one wavelength into another.
The color-plate citations refer to the original book, not to a newly supplied modern plate.
p0238#4.basis: Preserve ordered k=0, lambda, k and both literal Roman/numeric citation strings IV,1 and irregular IV2,3. Clarify source's stated central exception, same-order wavelength comparison and possible order overlap. No claim about uninspected plate colors, panels, ordering or availability; modern citation handling remains HOLD.

zh: **测量波长**：衍射光栅可以用来精确测量波长。
已知光栅常数后，测量某个主最大值对应的角 $\varphi$，并确认它属于哪个级次，就能利用前面的关系确定波长。
角度给出传播方向，已知的级次告诉我们程差包含多少个波长。
中心亮纹不能完成这种区分，因为各个波长在零级都指向正前方。
这种测量要使用可识别的非零级次，并符合推导中的入射条件。
en: **Measuring wavelength.** A diffraction grating can measure wavelength precisely.
With the grating spacing known, measure the angle $\varphi$ of a principal maximum and identify its order.
The earlier relation then determines the wavelength.
The angle gives the propagation direction, while the identified order tells how many wavelengths fit the path difference.
The central band cannot distinguish wavelengths this way, because every wavelength points straight ahead in the zero order.
Use an identifiable nonzero order and the incidence conditions of the derivation.
p0238#5.basis: Retain exact phi token and the known-grating-spacing angle-measurement method. Make identifying the order and excluding the nondispersive zero order explicit without adding an equation, example or practice task.

zh: **生活中的光栅现象**：原书用睫毛之间的间隔说明一种粗糙的光栅结构。
它记述，眯眼看明亮光源时会看到虹彩，这是白光在睫毛附近衍射并分开的现象。
这是一种现象说明，不需要直视强光来验证。
原书还把使用久了的唱片上靠得很近的沟纹，比作反射衍射光栅。
唱片反射电灯光时，可以看到光谱，有时还能看到对应不同 $k$ 值的几个光谱。
原书指出，当电灯光以比较大的入射角照到唱片上时，图样会很清晰。
这是斜入射的观察描述，不能直接把前面正入射推导的关系用于它。
沟纹的作用是让反射光按方向分布，彩色光不是唱片自己产生的新光。
en: **Grating effects in everyday objects.** The source uses the gaps between eyelashes as an example of a rough grating.
It describes rainbow-like colors seen while squinting at a bright source, caused by diffraction and separation of white light around the eyelashes.
This describes an observation, not a reason to stare at an intense light.
The source also compares the closely spaced grooves of a well-used record to a reflection diffraction grating.
Reflected lamp light can show a spectrum, and sometimes several spectra corresponding to different values of $k$.
The source says the pattern is especially clear when the lamp light strikes the record at a relatively large incidence angle.
That is an oblique-incidence observation, so the earlier normal-incidence relation cannot be applied to it without accounting for the changed incidence.
The grooves distribute reflected light among directions; the colored light is not newly created by the record.
p0238#6.basis: Retain eyelash gaps, rainbow observation, well-used record, reflected electric-lamp light, the exact k token, multiple spectra and the relatively large incidence-angle observation. Add no new experiment; explicitly separate this oblique-incidence observation from the preceding normal-incidence derivation.

sourceDiagramObservations.observation: A rectangular ruled surface has closely spaced parallel vertical strips. A round magnifying glass overlaps its lower-right area and shows those strips enlarged, with a visible handle. No numerical scale, slit count, or labeled a/b/d dimensions is printed inside this crop.
sourceDiagramObservations.explanatoryUse: Explain repeated narrow transparent/opaque structure, and identify the circular component as magnification rather than an additional optical screen or another grating.
sourceDiagramObservations.uncertainty: Monochrome scan does not independently identify which individual dark/light stroke is the transmitting slit, nor an exact strip count. Widths and transmission properties are supplied by the text.

sourceDiagramObservations.observation: Incoming arrows at left point horizontally to a vertical slit grating. A and B are corresponding edges of adjacent slits, and a vertical d dimension marks their separation. Rays leave toward the upper right, parallel before the vertical converging-lens symbol. At A a phi angle is shown against a horizontal normal. A dashed helper from B reaches C on the ray from A, making the path-difference triangle. Rays change direction at the lens and meet at a point on the vertical screen on the right.
sourceDiagramObservations.explanatoryUse: Explain normal incidence, corresponding slit points, repeat spacing d, outgoing angle measured from the normal, AC path difference and its right-triangle sine projection, then same-direction focusing at the screen.
sourceDiagramObservations.uncertainty: The source is schematic and has no focal length, grating-to-lens distance, lens-to-screen numerical distance, wavelength value, exact angle value, or calibrated intensity distribution. Interpret focal-plane placement from the source prose, not the drawn scale.

holds.reason: Both original source citations are retained, including the printed irregularity IV2,3. No plate was inspected or created. Modern citation/availability and the Roman/color-tool boundary require separate human-approved handling.
Raw PNG inspection informs explanatory text only. Modern figure creation and review are a separate delegation, not authorized or performed here.
This is the FIRST author candidate, not independent bilingual, scientific or pedagogical approval. Additional model qualifications are explicitly author explanations for independent review.

uncertainties: No external scientific or historical verification was attempted because the assignment is offline-only.

The source calls reflection gratings the best-quality type and describes white-gelatin impressions. These source statements are attributed and retained without a silent material-name correction or a newly asserted universal quality ranking.
Normal incidence is supplied by the inspected apparatus diagram; the source's later record example explicitly uses oblique incidence. No oblique-incidence equation was invented.
Single-slit modulation, possible weak or missing orders, finite allowed order directions and order overlap are authored scope clarifications, not source transcriptions or registered errata.
The source supplies no numerical wavelength, slit width, grating spacing, observation angle, focal length, screen distance or calibrated brightness.
